title: Folder parent map search has a fixed 100k limit, not paginated
answers: Folder migration validation misses folders in a very large instance
Why does folder tree validation silently drop folders beyond 100000?
body:
Symptom: folder-tree validation during migration can miss folders when an org/stack has more than 100,000 folders, since the search used to build the parent map uses a hard-coded Limit.
Root cause: pkg/storage/unified/migrations/validator.go:buildUnifiedFolderParentMap sends a single ResourceSearchRequest with Limit: 100000 and no pagination.
Fix pattern: reviewers explicitly rejected bumping the limit to 1,000,000; the agreed direction is to paginate the search (follow-up), not to raise the fixed constant.
Constraints: any future change to this function must add pagination (e.g. loop with continue tokens/offsets) rather than just increasing Limit, to correctly support arbitrarily large folder trees.
applies: pkg/storage/unified/migrations validator folder-tree search logic; any similar fixed-Limit full-table search in unified storage.
says: Folder migration validation misses folders in very large instances
Folder tree validation stops checking beyond a large size threshold
Very large folder trees incompletely validated during migration
Pagination needed for folder tree validation to handle large instances
search: Folder parent map search in pkg/storage/unified/migrations/validator.go:buildUnifiedFolderParentMap uses a hard-coded 100,000 Limit without pagination, causing migration validation to miss folders in orgs/stacks exceeding this threshold. The constraint is that future changes must add pagination (loop with continue tokens/offsets) rather than bumping the Limit constant, per reviewer decision. Applies to ResourceSearchRequest-based searches for full folder trees, including any similar fixed-Limit full-table search patterns in unified storage that require support for arbitrarily large datasets.
